name: ETP IAM
description: Reusable ETP capability providing human and service authentication (Keycloak-backed) and JWT-backed authorization checks against IAM PostgreSQL RBAC metadata. Independent Spring Boot service; not a business application.

version.description: Initial capability version documenting Phase 1 human login, client_credentials service tokens, and authorization checks. Excludes PKCE, refresh, logout, and admin APIs.

humanAuthentication.summary: Broker username/password to Keycloak via server-side confidential client (Direct Access Grant). Passwords are not stored in IAM.
humanAuthentication.caller: ETP Core UI and other human-facing consumers

serviceAuthentication.summary: Issue OAuth2 access tokens using client_credentials grant only.

authorization.summary: Evaluate whether a Bearer JWT principal is authorized for an application permission using IAM PostgreSQL RBAC metadata (principal, groups, roles, role_application_permissions).
authorization.optionalTenantScope: When tenant is provided on the request, group_tenant_assignments are enforced.

user.roles: array of strings (Keycloak realm roles from token)

apis.name: Service token
apis.response: OAuth2 token fields (access_token, token_type, expires_in, etc.)

requestBody.application: string (required) — IAM application code or name
requestBody.permission: string (required) — IAM permission code or name

errors.description: JWT valid but principal not authorized or inactive

openApi.note: Resolve OpenAPI location against the deployed IAM service base URL (default port 8081).

authentication: Access tokens are issued by Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth2).
IAM validates JWTs on protected routes via Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server using issuer-uri.
Human login uses a confidential Keycloak client; client secret is server-side in IAM only and must not be exposed to browsers.
Service authentication uses client_credentials; client_secret must be transmitted only over HTTPS in deployed environments.
Passwords are never persisted in IAM PostgreSQL or returned in API responses.
authorization: Authorization checks require a valid JWT with iss and sub matching an ACTIVE principals row in etp_iam.
RBAC chain: principal → group → role → role_application_permissions → application + permission.
Keycloak realm roles returned on login are not used for /authorization/check.
Optional tenant parameter gates access via group_tenant_assignments when provided.

requirements: PostgreSQL database etp_iam for authorization metadata
Keycloak realm with OIDC token endpoint and configured login/service clients
Environment-driven configuration; no secrets baked into the container image

nfr.availability: Service startup requires reachable PostgreSQL and Keycloak for readiness probes. IAM returns HTTP 502 when Keycloak token endpoint is unavailable during login/token requests.
nfr.performance: No published numeric SLOs in v1.0.0. Authorization checks are read-only database queries against IAM metadata.
nfr.scalability: Stateless Spring Boot service; horizontal scaling requires shared PostgreSQL, Keycloak, and consistent issuer configuration.
nfr.security: Secrets and credentials must be supplied via environment variables or a secret manager; HTTPS required for credential-bearing requests in deployed environments.
nfr.maintainability: IAM schema applied via Flyway migrations on service startup (V1 schema, optional V2 dev RBAC seed).

startupOrder: Keycloak (realm, clients, issuer URL reachable from IAM)
ETP IAM service (Flyway migrations then application listen)

indicators: keycloakRealm — HTTP GET realm metadata endpoint
db — Spring Boot datasource health (when enabled)

migrations: V2__platform_dev_seed.sql — optional development RBAC seed for Core UI

operations.configuration: All deployment settings are environment-driven; see configuration section.

implementedScope: Authorization via POST /api/v1/authorization/check with Bearer JWT

parameters.name: ETP_IAM_DB_URL
parameters.description: JDBC URL for etp_iam PostgreSQL database

parameters.name: ETP_IAM_DB_PASSWORD
parameters.description: Database password — supply via environment or secret manager

parameters.name: ETP_IAM_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_URI
parameters.description: JWT issuer URI (must match Keycloak realm)

parameters.name: ETP_IAM_KEYCLOAK_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID
parameters.description: Confidential client ID for human login broker

external.name: Keycloak
external.role: Identity provider; JWT issuance and credential validation
requirements: Realm configured with issuer matching ETP_IAM_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER_URI
Confidential login client for IAM broker (Direct Access Grants enabled for Phase 1 dev)

dependencies.note: PostgreSQL and Keycloak are external infrastructure, not registered ETP capabilities. Registry dependency entries (capabilityVersionId) are empty for v1.0.0.
